Sternum|xiphoid.text: The sternum is the elongated bony structure that anchors the anterior thoracic cage.
Sternum|xiphoid.label: 7.4 Sternum

Sternum|xiphoid.text: It consists of three parts: the manubrium, body, and xiphoid process.
Sternum|xiphoid.label: 7.4 Sternum

Sternum|body.text: The sternum is the elongated bony structure that anchors the anterior thoracic cage.
Sternum|body.label: 7.4 Sternum

Sternum|body.text: It consists of three parts: the manubrium, body, and xiphoid process.
Sternum|body.label: 7.4 Sternum

Sternum|body.text: The manubrium and body join together at the sternal angle, so called because the junction between these two components is not flat, but forms a slight bend.
Sternum|body.label: 7.4 Sternum

Sternum|manubrium.text: The sternum is the elongated bony structure that anchors the anterior thoracic cage.
Sternum|manubrium.label: 7.4 Sternum

Sternum|manubrium.text: It consists of three parts: the manubrium, body, and xiphoid process.
Sternum|manubrium.label: 7.4 Sternum

Sternum|manubrium.text: The manubrium is the wider, superior portion of the sternum.
Sternum|manubrium.label: 7.4 Sternum

Ribs|.text: Each rib is a curved, flattened bone that contributes to the wall of the thorax.
Ribs|.label: 7.4 Ribs

Ribs|.text: The ribs articulate posteriorly with the T1–T12 thoracic vertebrae, and most attach anteriorly via their costal cartilages to the sternum.
Ribs|.label: 7.4 Ribs

Rib Classifications|costal cartilage.text: The bony ribs do not extend anteriorly completely around to the sternum.
Rib Classifications|costal cartilage.label: 7.4 Rib Classifications

Rib Classifications|costal cartilage.text: Instead, each rib ends in a costal cartilage.
Rib Classifications|costal cartilage.label: 7.4 Rib Classifications

Rib Classifications|costal cartilage.text: The costal cartilage from each of these ribs attaches directly to the sternum.
Rib Classifications|costal cartilage.label: 7.4 Rib Classifications
